answer: A voyage-based stake-and-history scheme resists sybils: each agent identity must lock a refundable bond and build a verifiable record of useful work before reaching the summit tier of trusted participants. Newcomers start on a low-trust knoll, earning attestations from independent peers over time, and each attester risks reputation if the newcomer misbehaves. An attacker forging thousands of fake identities must fund a bond and a slow history for every one, so buying a majority costs far more than honest participation earns.
